why.Cathedral Driveway trail #510A from Loom: When coming from the east side or wanting the least climbing of the long trails; it starts near Loomis and joins the Chewuch valley trail to the same Cathedral Lakes basin.
why.Thirtymile Trailhead and the Chewuch Riv: When linking the Remmel Lake country with the climb; it is a longer walk up the Chewuch valley than the Andrews Creek line but ends in the same basin.

review.notes: No way marked; the first entry covers the Andrews Creek line, the shortest drive and best documented. Searches found no source naming the Driveway trail or ranking the trails, so both reasons lean on stored notes.
fromStoredNotes: Cathedral Driveway trail #510A from Loomis via Toats Coulee
Thirtymile Trailhead and the Chewuch River trail toward Remmel Lake

problems: Primary chosen from weak evidence; the first way in is a generic camp-and-slope entry that stands for three trails.
primary pick withdrawn in review: the evidence was weak, so no Most used mark is claimed

why.Early-season snow to the Concord-Lexingt: Early season, from when the highway opens until late June, while the gully to the col still holds firm snow that buries the boot path; bring an axe, and crampons if it is refrozen.

review.notes: Reports agree on one approach; the snow variant is the same line in early summer, with the gully usually snow-filled until late June.

why.Pacific Crest Trail north from Harts Pas: When no boat is available and you want to stay in the United States; it is about 27 miles each way along the crest from Harts Pass, which usually opens only in July.

review.notes: Search confirmed Freezeout Creek (west), Crow Creek (east) and north approaches exist; nothing tied a north-face approach to Harts Pass, so that reason rests on stored notes. The northern border-crossing way was left without a reason on purpose.
fromStoredNotes: Pacific Crest Trail north from Harts Pass

problems: The northern provincial-park approach crosses the border away from a port of entry, so no why was written; the owner may want it removed or reworded.
The Harts Pass PCT approach could not be corroborated online.

why.From the east: Ross Lake water taxi to L: When starting from the SR-20 side or linking a Pickets traverse out to Ross Lake; it skips the long Hannegan drive but needs a water taxi booked ahead from the resort.

review.notes: Both ways reach Whatcom Pass at similar mileage (about 17 miles); the Hannegan side as primary is consistent with the prior note.

wa_north_ridge_3.primary: The SR-20 South Buttress pullout, then bear right into the basin beneath the North Ridge Notch

why.Rainy Pass and Porcupine Creek into the: When camped near Rainy Pass or combining objectives; longer than the highway-side basin but simple to navigate, with cleaner rock and two or three short low-fifth pitches to the notch.

review.notes: The highway pullout approach is shared with the South Buttress and is the standard and shorter; the Rainy Pass line is the published alternative.

why.Cutthroat Lake and Cutthroat Pass: When starting from the Cutthroat Pass trailhead on the highway or combining with a Cutthroat Pass hike; it is mostly maintained trail, then about a mile of rotten ridge scrambling south from the pass.

review.notes: The Rainy Pass line from the PCT is the listed main approach; the Cutthroat Pass crest is the second option.

why.Lyman Lakes basin to the south flank: When the Railroad Creek corridor is open again and you prefer the ferry and shuttle to crossing Spider Gap, whose glacier travel and steep climb it avoids.

review.notes: Most online reports reach Lyman Lakes from Phelps Creek over Spider Gap; stored notes say the Railroad Creek corridor is closed. No source describes the east route itself.
fromStoredNotes: Lyman Lakes basin to the south flank

problems: Primary chosen on the Railroad Creek closure plus Phelps Creek being the commonly reported start; the first way in's name describes a basin and its notes cover both ways in.

why.Big Beaver Trail to Luna Camp, then the: When starting from SR-20 and wanting the shortest, flattest way into the Pickets; the water taxi and Big Beaver trail are easy, but the last stretch up Luna Creek is a pathless bushwhack.

review.notes: Luna Creek is described as the shortest, flattest but roughest way into the Pickets; Whatcom and Perfect Pass is the more established. No Phantom-specific comparison found.

why.Entiat River trail and Snow Brushy Creek: When you want mostly maintained trail and reliable water at Snow Brushy Creek; it ends at Borealis Pass below the easy south slopes, though burned timber can hide the last faint trail.

review.notes: The Snow Brushy Creek approach is well documented online and described as easier than the Sheep Driveway line.

problems: Snow Brushy Creek and Borealis Pass is the better documented approach online and may be at least as common as the marked primary.

wa_primus_peak_south_ridge.primary: The far end of the Eldorado ice cap: five glaciers and a notch at the McAllister-Klawatti col

why.Thunder Creek and the Borealis Glacier:: When you want a shorter two-day trip with fewer glaciers and fewer people; it costs a cold Thunder Creek crossing and brush, and it finishes on the east ridge, not this south side.

review.notes: The Eldorado way is the one that reaches this route's south side; Thunder Creek is the well-reported line for Primus overall but leads to a different line.

problems: The Thunder Creek way in finishes on the east ridge, not this route; Thunder Creek may be the most used way to climb Primus in general.

why.Snow Lakes and the lower Enchantments: Chosen to avoid the loose scree grind of Aasgard Pass; the Snow Lakes trail is longer but gentler and shaded on hot days, and it makes an easy walk out.

review.notes: Aasgard Pass is the more common, shorter but steeper; Snow Lakes is longer, gentler and shaded.
